description: What `softory gate` checks before a unit of work may move to done. The RACI in raci.md is the human-readable source; keep both in step.

review.description: A review run kept as its own task, so the reviewer can claim it and attach the report. Its for:<ID> tags name the tasks it reviewed. The verdicts live as review records on those tasks, so the review itself is not reviewed again.

legacy.description: Tasks with no unit: tag, usually created before softory joined the project. They keep the project's own process; softory close holds them to this minimum. softory adopt turns one into a unit.

rules.no_self_review: For a review entry marked not_self, and for every tag review, a reviewer who is assigned to or holds the claim on the task never counts. Greg's acceptance of a story or epic he owns is an acceptance, not a self code review, so it counts.
rules.evidence_required: At least one evidence row (the CLI enforces this too).
rules.blocks_resolved: Every active blocks dependency must point at a done task or be resolved.
rules.if_builder: When everyone a tag review names built the task (Toby wrote the threat model, Quinn built the architecture change), the tag's if_builder reviewers review it instead: Quinn for Toby's own security work, Jade or Gold for Quinn's architecture work, the owner for Darwin's own design work. The owner chose this on 2026-10-23.
rules.review_units: A review unit closes when it has evidence and, for each for:<ID> tag, its builder has recorded a review on that task. Tag reviews do not apply to it, and nobody reviews the review.
rules.stand_ins: An agent the owner names with softory standin add counts wherever the roles it stands in for count, as a reviewer or a closer. Stand-ins live in .agents/softory/local.json and each change is recorded as a decision.
